# Welcome {.unnumbered}

This is the replication guide for

> **Cluster-Aware Uncertainty for Polytomous Mokken Scalability:
> A Calibrated Hierarchical Bayesian Bootstrap.**
> JoonHo Lee (2026). arXiv preprint (identifier forthcoming).

It walks through the package that rebuilds every number, figure and table in
the paper.

**Almost no external data.** One thing you need is the `mokken` package, which
carries the application data; everything else ships. Clone, run four commands,
and all 15 exhibits rebuild in about five seconds.

## Quick start

```bash
Rscript 00_setup.R                          # reports what's missing; installs nothing
Rscript exhibits/00_build_all.R             # 7 figures + 8 floats + the ledger, ~5s
Rscript verification/verify_reproduction.R  # 16 / 16
bash verification/cold_start_rehearsal.sh   # everything, from a bare copy
```

R ≥ 4.1 and eleven CRAN packages — **including `mokken`, which is required
here** rather than optional, because the application data `SWMDK` is
distributed inside it and no responses ship with this package.

## What is reproduced

- **All 15 published exhibits.** The eight LaTeX floats are byte-identical to
  what the paper prints; the seven figures match on page geometry and a
  fixed-DPI render hash.
- **The 144-key ledger, byte-identical** to the one the manuscript was verified
  against.
- **All 69 of the manuscript's concordance predicates**, re-expressed against
  the *rebuilt* ledger.

## What is *not* reproduced

The Phase 16 confirmation and the Phase 17 application. Both ran on AWS; the
pipeline ships as annotated reference code and is documented rather than
enabled.

## What you can check

| Question | Where |
|---|---|
| Do the exhibits follow from the data? | [Exhibits](06-exhibits.qmd) |
| Does the data follow from a documented pipeline? | [Pipeline](05-pipeline.qmd) |
| Was the pipeline tuned after seeing results? | [Governance](08-governance.qmd) |
| **Does an independent implementation agree?** | [the oracle lane](09-reproducibility.qmd#the-independent-oracle-lane) |

That last one is unusually strong here. The oracle lane recomputes **Koopman et
al. (2022)'s published results** from the same data and reproduces them, and it
confirms that a linear-programming solution of the transport problem agrees with
the two-pointer implementation the method uses across an exhaustive grid.

## One thing to know before reading the code

`reference-code/R/core/ordinal-h.R` ships with a **known archival defect** and a
prominent "do not port" banner. Its transport helper advances on a 1e-12 mass
tolerance and can drop a valid tiny positive mass; the corrected kernel is in
the `bayesmokken` package.

No locked result is affected, and this package **checks that** rather than
asserting it: across the 48 locked truth rows, the number with a gap in the
open interval (0, 1e-12) — the only condition under which the defect can fire —
is **zero**. See [reproducibility](09-reproducibility.qmd#the-archival-defect).

## Companion package

The binary, independent-respondent case has its own package:
[`bayesmokken-scalability-replication`](https://github.com/joonho112/bayesmokken-scalability-replication).

Neither depends on the other and they share no data. They do share the
verification harness, byte-for-byte, because this package ports it.
